## R isn't a list of commands — it's a small language

You don't need to memorize R. You need to recognize three pieces of grammar, because once you can read them, most R code becomes a sentence instead of a puzzle.

Every example below is **live** — click into the code and press **Run**, or just edit it and run your own version. Nothing you do here can break anything.

## 1. Objects: labelled boxes

```r
age <- 25
```

Read `<-` as **"store this, under this name."** This line means: *take the number 25, put it in a box, label the box `age`.* From now on, typing `age` anywhere gets you back what's in the box.

<p class="rr-try-live">🌐 Try it live — run it, then change 25 to your own age and run it again</p>

```{webr-r}
age <- 25
age

age <- 30   # relabel the box with a new value
age
```

::: {.callout-note}
## Why the arrow, not `=`?
`age = 25` also works in R, but `<-` is the convention, and it's worth keeping: it visually points in the direction the value is flowing — *into* the box.
:::

## 2. Functions: verbs that need ingredients

```r
mean(age)
```

A function name followed by parentheses is a **verb** — and whatever's inside the parentheses are its **ingredients** (arguments). Read `mean(age)` as *"compute the mean, using `age` as the ingredient."* Some verbs need more than one ingredient, separated by commas — `round(3.14159, 2)` reads as *"round 3.14159, to 2 decimal places."*

<p class="rr-try-live">🌐 Try it live</p>

```{webr-r}
age <- 25
mean(age)
round(3.14159, 2)
```

## 3. Vectors: R's basic unit

R rarely stores just one thing — it stores **vectors**, which are just ordered collections of values of the same type. Here's the twist: a single number, like the `age` above, actually *is* a vector — one with a length of 1. That's why functions like `mean()` work the same way whether you give them one number or a thousand.

<p class="rr-try-live">🌐 Try it live</p>

```{webr-r}
ages <- c(25, 31, 28, 40)   # c() = "combine these into one vector"
mean(ages)
ages[1]                      # square brackets = "give me item number..."
```

## Try it: translate before you run

Before you run this one, write in plain English (out loud, or in your head) what each line does. Then run it and check yourself against the last two lines.

<p class="rr-try-live">🌐 Try it live</p>

```{webr-r}
name <- "Anna"
n_participants <- 42
scores <- c(88, 92, 79)
mean_score <- mean(scores)
first_score <- scores[1]

mean_score
first_score
```
